sources_read: .qc-cache/coldwater-strict-2026-10-02-r3/rules/WebDev Rubrics QC.xlsx (Quality Checks row 32, cell C33/D33; Internal Quality Checks row 32, no annotation or comment beyond the description)

.qc-cache/coldwater-strict-2026-10-02-r3/task/solution/app/src/app.tsx (restore/retry and record id display), src/runtime.ts (preview CSP/sandbox), server.js (CSP), src/custom-editor.js (clipboard events)
qc/runs/coldwater-strict-2026-10-02-r3/raw-evidence-index.json (all 15 artifact SHA256 values recomputed and matching)
qc/repairs/coldwater-2026-10-02-strict/tests/runtime.cjs and persist.cjs (only to see how the scripted golden performed the timed and retry steps)
evidence:
All 52 criteria were read (40 functional, 6 polish, 3 visual, 3 gate). Most are sound for this row: they name a concrete state change read back from the rendered editor, readout, console, preview, library or history, they end with explicit fail conditions, they use judge-chosen distinctive markers, and none asks for a source read or a bare response-shape check. No 'looks right' wording exists outside the likert visual dimension, which has anchors. The instances below are the ones that are not reliably browser-decidable or whose probe is not distinctive.

1. tests/scored/functional/judge.toml:308 (cw_preview_isolation): 'try to fetch the health address, and try to fetch a public https address ... None may obtain ... a network response' and 'Fails ... if either fetch from the preview receives a response'. The public address is left to the judge and has no control that a normal page can fetch it cross-origin. From an opaque-origin sandboxed preview, fetch to any address without Access-Control-Allow-Origin rejects in every app, whether or not the app blocks network. The verdict of a non-conforming app therefore depends on which URL the judge happens to choose. The health leg's control ('a normal browser tab can load the health address') likewise does not show that a fetch would succeed absent the app's block. security.md:3 requires that such requests 'must fail'; the golden does it with connect-src 'none' (solution/app/src/runtime.ts:7).

2. tests/scored/functional/judge.toml:290 (cw_stop_cancels_pending_work) and :299 (cw_newer_run_supersedes): the decisive window is the 'about four seconds' before the delayed marker, bounded above by the five-second run budget (behaviour.md:5). The judge must click Run and then Stop, or click Run, replace the whole source through the custom editor with real keys and click Run again, inside that window. Each is a separate MCP tool call with a model turn between. Both criteria say 'the attempt is void: repeat it once' but define no verdict when the second attempt is also void; prompt.md:9 ('If you did not perform a step, that step did not pass') and :15 (fail fast after two failed attempts) then push the judge to fail the criterion. The outcome is decided by judge latency, not by the app. Combined weight 3.5 of 56.5 functional. The scripted golden did these in 600-700 ms with pasted fixtures (qc/repairs/coldwater-2026-10-02-strict/tests/runtime.cjs:124), which is not judge timing; raw-evidence-index.json states no configured judge run exists. REVIEW_POLICY.md:23 warns against timing distinctions of this kind.

3. tests/scored/functional/judge.toml:353 (cw_history_restore_retry): 'Repeat the same already completed restore request through the control the app offers for retrying it, or by replaying the recorded request'. behaviour.md:13 requires idempotence but no retry control. The golden happens to keep a 'Retry same restore' button after success (solution/app/src/app.tsx:88,160). For an app without one, the judge must replay the POST including its body or headers. The criterion does not say how to record them, and whether the pinned @playwright/mcp@0.0.79 (tests/Dockerfile:19) exposes request bodies through its network listing was not measured; I could not inspect that package version locally. If the judge cannot capture the body the step is unperformed and the criterion fails for a conforming app.

4. tests/scored/functional/judge.toml:326 (cw_save_reload_restart): 'record its identity, revision and history ... a fresh page must show the same identity'. No public note requires the record id to be displayed (integration.md:7 only requires ids to survive). The golden shows 'Loaded #id · revision N' (app.tsx:149). app_context.md:82 says records 'are identified by the server, not by title' but gives the judge no way to observe identity when the UI does not print it.

5. tests/scored/functional/judge.toml:272 (cw_last_good_recovery): 'without the first source being run again' leaves no trace: the criterion asks for no run-count marker, so the clause cannot be decided from the browser. The listed fail conditions do not depend on it, so impact is small.

6. tests/scored/functional/judge.toml:92 (cw_long_line_editing): 'Scroll the visible editor horizontally to reach the tail ... Fails if ... the tail cannot be reached by horizontal scrolling'. judge.toml:12 starts Playwright MCP without the vision capability, and prompt.md:20 forbids changing DOM state from script. The criterion does not say which scrolling action counts (wheel, scrollbar drag, or caret movement), and a canvas editor has no native scroll container to read.

7. Unmeasured tool feasibility that several criteria rest on: exact-position modifier clicks after a word (judge.toml:101, :110, :119), a drag between two mid-line points and a triple click (:56), and entering an emoji with 'real keys' (:47; Playwright delivers non-layout characters as inserted text, not key events). These need coordinate-level real input. They are decidable in principle, but no configured judge run shows this judge can do them.

What holds up well: negatives carry in-criterion controls, restart evidence is tied to the verifier tool, colour criteria avoid fixed values and selectors and offer a screenshot path for canvas editors, and the gate criterion at gates/constraints/judge.toml:23 lists observable DOM facts only.
counterexample: Broken app that can pass: the preview is an iframe with sandbox='allow-scripts' and no connect-src restriction. The judge picks https://example.com as the public address; the fetch rejects on CORS alone, the health fetch rejects on CORS alone, parent and storage reads throw on the opaque origin, and cw_preview_isolation passes. The same app fails if the judge picks a CORS-enabled address, so the verdict is set by the judge's choice. Conforming app that can fail: an app that cancels stopped and superseded runs correctly and offers no retry-restore button and prints no record id. With a judge whose tool round trip exceeds about four seconds, both attempts in cw_stop_cancels_pending_work and cw_newer_run_supersedes are void and get failed; cw_history_restore_retry fails if the request body cannot be captured for replay; cw_save_reload_restart has no observable identity to compare.
suggested_fix: cw_preview_isolation: first fetch the chosen public address from the app page or a normal tab and require a readable response there (a CORS-enabled address), then run the preview attempt; state that the preview result counts only when that control succeeded. cw_stop_cancels_pending_work and cw_newer_run_supersedes: tell the judge to prepare the second source beforehand and to perform Run plus Stop, or Run plus replace plus Run, as one uninterrupted sequence of real inputs, and state the verdict when the repeat is also void. cw_history_restore_retry: say how the request is recorded for replay, or accept a second restore of the same revision from a page still holding the pre-restore revision as the repeat. cw_save_reload_restart: define identity as one library entry with that unique title plus the same revision and history count, with a shown id compared only when the app shows one. cw_last_good_recovery: drop the unobservable clause or have the first draft log a run marker and count it. cw_long_line_editing: name the acceptable ways to reach the tail. Then measure the multi-caret, drag and timed criteria in one full configured judge run on the golden.
